Subject: Operator onboarding — request for topology, isolation controls, and threat summary

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of our procurement/segmentation review we need a short packet that explains how Redwood treats operator accounts and where operator-run components can reach customer dataplane and control plane surfaces. Specifically StraitsBank's security team is asking for:

- A diagram that shows control plane vs dataplane boundaries for a typical private deployment (high-level is fine).
- A short table describing which operator services have inbound/outbound network privileges (and to which endpoints).
- A 1-2 page threat model summary that explains mitigations for operator lateral movement and data exfiltration.

Our timeline is tight — can you provide an initial package by end of day Wednesday (PST)? If some items require redaction we can accept sanitized artifacts and a follow-up bridge call.

Regards,

Ben —

Attaching an initial evidence packet that should cover the items you listed. Quick notes:

- redwood_topology_sketch_v1.png is a sanitized topology (no customer IPs) showing control plane, operator management plane (hosted control), and dataplane (customer VPC / on-prem inference clusters).
- redwood_operator_isolation_matrix.xlsx lists operator roles, the minimum network privileges we grant for each role, and the compensating controls (KMS, session recording, privileged session broker).
- threat_model_summary_straits_v1.pdf is a short narrative: attack surface, likely operator misuse scenarios, and our standard mitigations (least privilege, ephemeral creds, KV cache safeguards, egress allowlisting).

Two quick clarifications we should confirm with your team before finalizing:
1) For private deployments, do you require outbound-only bastioning (no incoming operator-initiated connections into customer subnets)? We included both patterns in the packet but flagged recommended settings.
2) Please confirm whether you want full high-res diagrams via Drive (sensitive) or only embedded PNGs for the RFP. I included a Drive link for the high-res diagram — access can be restricted.

Markus and Marissa — can you quickly validate the phrasing in the threat summary and add anything about our continuous audit hooks? Priya — if you have a sample configuration that shows the bastionless mode, please attach.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Operator onboarding — request for topology, isolation controls, and threat summary

Ben / Lauren —

Quick follow-up with details and one optional control we recommend for regulated tenants. Highlights below; full text is in the attached spreadsheet and PDF.

1) Operator network model (summary) - Operator management plane is logically separated from customer dataplane. In hosted mode this is a multi-tenant control plane running in Redwood-managed VPCs; operator consoles access telemetry and orchestration APIs over authenticated mTLS channels.

2) Privilege and egress constraints - Operator service accounts are scoped to the minimum required OAuth scopes and are constrained by VPC egress ACLs. For private deployments we support both:
  a) Bastion-mode: operator sessions originate from a temporary bastion host inside the customer-managed perimeter (recommended when inbound control is permitted).
  b) Outbound-only (preferred for maximum isolation): customer clusters initiate a short-lived outbound tunnel to our operator ingress that exposes a narrow management API over mTLS; operator cannot initiate arbitrary inbound connections.

3) Threat mitigations for operator lateral movement - Ephemeral credentials for operator tooling (rotated per session). - Session recording + immutable audit logs shipped to the customer's chosen KMS/S3. - Network egress allowlists combined with eBPF-based process attestation on inference nodes to limit toolset.

Inline ASCII sketch (sanitized):

Customer VPC  [Inference Nodes] <--(short-lived TLS tunnel)-- [Operator Ingress - Redwood VPC]
                 |
                 +-> [Private Storage / KMS] (egress allowlist)

4) Optional hardened posture (for financial services): require customer-managed bastion for operator sessions, and prohibit our operator accounts from connecting to admin ports directly. This adds operational friction but aligns with some auditors' expectations.

Links: high-res diagram (internal drive): https://drive.redwood.com/Shared/StraitsBank/Topology/highres-diagram.png
RFP checklist item id: HB-SEC-042 (see HubSpot deal)

Action items: Lauren to deliver the sanitized packet to Ben (done). Priya to attach a sample outbound-tunnel config if StraitsBank wants the outbound-only option (Priya, can you add by EOD?). Markus to prepare short talking points for a technical bridge call.

-Markus Klein
